content: Fine words and an insinuating appearance are seldom associated with true virtue.
author: Confucius
explanation: Excessive charm, polished flattery, and theatrical sweetness often conceal hollow character or predatory intent. Genuine virtue is usually quiet, unadorned, and grounded in plain truth.
practicalInsight: Look beyond surface charisma when assessing the trustworthiness of associates; evaluate their consistent track record of reliability.
reflectionPrompt: Have you ever been swayed by polished flattery over quiet substance, and what did that teach you?
